newsitem.title: USA: FCC's Hundt wants new laws to spur phone competition.
newsitem.headline: FCC's Hundt wants new laws to spur phone competition.

text.p: Eighteen months after passage of a major communications law, the nation's top phone regulator said Thursday that new laws were needed to open the $100 billion local phone market because it remains closed to competition.
"We have a major challenge to introduce competition into local telephone markets. And that challenge is not being met," outgoing Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said.
Hundt offered several recommendations for how "Congress can blow away the paralyzing fog the legal culture is spreading over the legislative and executive mandates to open the local market."

Speaking to a conference sponsored by the American Enterprise Institute, he urged Congress to pass legislation so that legal challenges to last year's communications act would be heard by one federal court. Currently, legal challenges to the act are scattered in courts across the nation.

The FCC chairman also urged lawmakers to give his agency national enforcement powers so that regulators could impose stiffer penalties to companies that violate FCC rules. And he called for Congress to order the courts to defer to the FCC when hearing challenges to the agency's rules.

Hundt complained that the many court challenges to his agency's interpretation of last year's law has slowed investment by long-distance companies and others seeking to enter the local phone business.
